content.introduction: The United States indicators show a mixed economic picture as of November 4, 2026. Business Confidence stands at 54.5 points, slightly down from 54.6 in the previous month. The Manufacturing PMI is at 55.9 points, up from 53.9, while the Non Manufacturing PMI is at 54.9 points, down from 55.4. The Services PMI is at 58.8 points, up from 56.5. The Composite PMI is at 58.4 points, up from 56. The Government Budget deficit is at -5.9% of GDP, up from -6.3%. The Conference Board Coincident Economic Index® (CEI) increased by 0.3% in September 2026 to 115.3 (2016=100), while the Leading Economic Index® (LEI) remained unchanged at 99.6 (2016=100).

The Conference Board Coincident Economic Index® (CEI) for the US increased by 0.3% in September 2026 to 115.3 (2016=100), following a 0.1% increase in August. Overall, the CEI rose by 0.9% over the six months between March and September 2026, up from its 0.2% growth over the previous six months. The CEI’s four component indicators—payroll employment, personal income less transfer payments, manufacturing and trade sales, and industrial production—are included among the data used to determine [...] The four components of the Coincident Economic Index® for the US are:

 Payroll employment
 Personal income less transfer payments
 Manufacturing and trade sales
 Industrial production

About The Conference Board [...] The Conference Board Leading Economic Index® (LEI) for the US was unchanged in September 2026 at 99.6 (2016=100), after a decline of 0.1% in August. The LEI grew by 0.6% between March and September 2026, a reversal from its decline of 1.1% over the previous six months (September 2025 to March 2026).

Contains a wide range of historical data from the earliest times to the present. Tables cover specific indicators such as employment, income, saving, poverty, construction, housing, consumer price indexes, and others.
